reasons: Mungbean (N-fixing) precedes wheat, adding residual nitrogen ahead of a heavy feeder.
Four different plant families across the rotation breaks pest/disease cycles.
Chickpea after cotton gives the soil a second legume break and needs little irrigation.
Shallow-to-deep rooting alternation (mungbean -> wheat -> cotton -> chickpea) improves soil structure at multiple depths.
Sorghum is markedly drought-tolerant, lowering irrigation need in the hottest season.
Berseem clover (N-fixing cover/fodder) rebuilds soil nitrogen and organic matter ahead of cotton.
Wheat closes the rotation on residual moisture and clover nitrogen credit.
warnings: Berseem clover yields no grain income; factor in fodder value separately.
